city_center.name: Portland Farmers Market (PSU) + the Willamette River
city_center.landmark: the Portland Farmers Market at Portland State University; the Willamette River bridges; Mount Hood on the eastern horizon; the Willamette Valley farm belt to the south
city_center.notes: The Portland Farmers Market at PSU is the flagship of a strong local-food city. Portland sits on the Willamette River with Mount Hood on the horizon and the fertile Willamette Valley -- berry, hazelnut, and pinot country -- to the south. sources: en.wikipedia.org Portland, Oregon; portlandfarmersmarket.org.

cultural_notes: Portland is a strong local-food city; the PSU Portland Farmers Market anchors a network sourcing the Willamette Valley -- marionberry, blueberry, hazelnut, and pinot country (source: portlandfarmersmarket.org; Willamette Valley agriculture framing)

the marionberry (an Oregon-bred blackberry) and the Oregon hazelnut (Oregon grows the vast majority of US hazelnuts) are signature state crops (source: Oregon State University / Oregon Hazelnut Industry framing, publicly documented)
Mount Hood (Timberline, Mt. Hood Meadows, Skibowl) is a short drive east, giving Portland a genuine ski and year-round-glacier-skiing adjacency (source: Mount Hood ski geography, publicly documented)
Fred Meyer (an Oregon-founded one-stop chain), WinCo (an employee-owned value grocer), and New Seasons (a local natural grocer) are the metro grocers (source: chain regional footprint)
